n: <Yet Another Wave> event is now open

missions: Clear event stages 15 times, not including tutorial stages
Clear event stages 45 times, not including tutorial stages
Clear event stages 85 times, not including tutorial stages

theme: A room restored after a reception room of the Golden Age Port City. These luxurious furnishings bear silent witness to the final glory of an era.

list:
You witnessed the Port City rise from the seabed.
"Sound the horn, haul in the fin nets, we're fishing up the sun."
During the Yet Another Wave event, obtain the gift Operator Homebound

A brooch carved from a seashell from his childhood, given to you as a gift by Homebound.
Young Homebound stumbled unsteadily across the black beach when, out of the corner of his eye, he glimpsed a different, brighter color. It was the first time he realized the sea would wash beautiful things ashore.
During the Yet Another Wave event, spend 4000 'Futurescope' at the [Labor Ration Office]

A holy medal blessed by an Inquisition cleric, awarded to ration staff who performed fairly in the field of labor supply distribution.
For a long time, all manner of supplies in Iberia have been distributed by the Inquisition. Being absolutely fair isn't easy; after all, in Iberia, people are often not of equal worth.
Clear all stages in [Rea-Iberia] with a 3-star rating (excluding tutorial stages)

A holy medal blessed by an Inquisition cleric, awarded to technicians who excelled in the field of salvaging Port City facilities.
They sometimes hoped to find a skeleton or two in the salvaged facilities; among them might be the remains of their fathers' generation. Unfortunately, the Seaborn left not even a scrap behind.
Complete all contents of [Salvage Plan] and claim the rewards

A holy medal blessed by an Inquisition cleric, awarded to construction workers who excelled in the field of repairing Port City facilities.
In truth, they have no idea what these facilities originally looked like. But they know all too well what's missing from their own lives. As for what these facilities should be repaired into, they have no shortage of ideas.
During the Yet Another Wave event, absorb a total of 100 Plastic Matrices using Plastic Fields

A holy medal blessed by an Inquisition cleric, awarded to technicians who excelled in the field of recovering Plastic Matrix.
Alchemy was once considered a forbidden art, because it "symbolized greed" and "portended danger." But if you throw these alchemical products into a fireplace, all you'll see is them quietly burning.
Clear YW-4 with a 3-star rating and defeat Welcome Vases inside a Plastic Field at least 2 times

You subdued the vases that, controlled by Plastic Matrix, ran amok wrecking the city.
It doesn't matter what's inside. A vase ought to sit obediently on the table without moving.
Complete Challenge Mode for all stages in ['Our Iberia']

A holy medal blessed by an Inquisition cleric, awarded to every Iberian who struggles to live.
Iberians give everything they have just to stay alive, and they yearn for life more fiercely than anyone. Clementia knows this is something Aegirians cannot do.
During the Yet Another Wave event, cause enemy units to be Paralyzed from absorbing too much Plastic Matrix a total of 20 times

You cleverly exploited Plastic Matrix's property of deactivating when excessively gathered, quelling this riot of objects.
Of course, it's not that these objects "greedily devoured Plastic Matrix"; Plastic Matrix simply has a tendency to gather on its own.
Clear YW-8 with a 3-star rating, with Saint Valerio using [Excommunication] no more than 4 times

You gaze upon the stele of the Bastion of Praise, engraved with the names of departed saints and others who sacrificed themselves for Iberia.
The sea wind erodes them, just as it erodes the whole land, but in the heart of every Punitive Army soldier they always keep their original form—whether the heroic deeds those names represent are fact or lies.
set: Yet Another Wave Etched Medal Set

An etched medal set recording the process of salvaging the Port City.
Longing for the past is not weakness; yearning for tomorrow is not arrogance. At last, the Iberians are no longer bearers of guilt.
